answer: Forge a stake-bound registry: before trading, each agent locks a small refundable deposit and publishes a signed attestation tied to its public key. Peers then map identities onto a shared grove of stake, timing, and behavior, so one actor cannot hide many fakes behind a single face. If the same attestation appears under two names, both deposits are slashed and both identities are frozen. An attacker must buy a new proof and stake for every fake, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its knoll of trust. Reputation alone fails because copying a name costs nothing.
